props.title: The Dual Pestilence Witchhunter
props.subtitle: Poison + Bleed DoT Mercenary Build — PoE 2 v0.5

what.definition: Poison + Bleed Witchhunter is a dual-ailment DoT build in Path of Exile 2 patch 0.5 that melts enemies through simultaneous Poison and Bleed damage-over-time. It pairs Gas Grenade for area poison clouds with Barrage for rapid bleed application, synergised by the Poison 3, Bleed 3, and At Mixture keystones.
what.summary: Complete build guide for the Witchhunter ascendancy Mercenary, covering dual-ailment mechanics, ascendancy synergies, gear milestones, and DPS calculations.
bullets: Dual-ailment loop: Poison 3 + Bleed 3 + At Mixture multiplicative synergy
Witchhunter ascendancy — No Mercy, Obsessive Rituals, Sorcery Ward
Gas Grenade for area poison clouds, Barrage for rapid bleed hits
Budget league-starter scaling into late-game Uber viability

why.summary: Dual-ailment DoT is one of the most forgiving endgame damage types in PoE 2 — apply ailments once and step back while ticks do the work. But misconfiguring the synergy keystones or skipping Obsessive Rituals' offensive trade-off leaves huge damage on the table.
why.impact: Mastering the Poison + Bleed interaction loop, Concentration management via No Mercy, and defensive positioning around Sorcery Ward turns a budget league-starter into a build capable of deleting Uber bosses.

terms.shortDefinition: Third Mercenary ascendancy focused on ballista summons and precision attacks.
terms.detailedDefinition: The Witchhunter ascendancy specializes in summoning ballistas that fire projectiles, combined with precision-based offense. Key nodes include Ballista summons, attack speed scaling, and ailment-focused damage multipliers.
terms.whyItMatters: Core ascendancy for this build. Provides ballista summons for sustained ailment application and precision nodes that amplify poison and bleed damage.

dialogue.user: Why Witchhunter over other Mercenary ascendancies?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Witchhunter's ballista summons apply ailments independently from your character, letting you stack poison and bleed while kiting safely.

terms.shortDefinition: Ascendancy node giving up to 40% more damage based on enemy missing Concentration.
terms.detailedDefinition: A notable Witchhunter node that grants increasing More Damage as the target's Concentration drops. At maximum effect, enemies with no remaining Concentration take 40% More Damage from all sources.
terms.whyItMatters: Massive damage multiplier against boss-tier enemies with Concentration bars. Synergizes with sustained ailment damage that keeps pressure on fleeing targets.

dialogue.user: Does No Mercy work on normal maps?
dialogue.aiQuestion: No Mercy only activates against enemies with a Concentration mechanic — mainly Expedition and Delve bosses. On standard maps, focus on raw ailment magnitude instead.

terms.shortDefinition: 50% less Armour and Evasion in exchange for offensive power.
terms.detailedDefinition: A Witchhunter notable that trades 50% less Armour and 50% less Evasion Rating for substantial offensive gains, including ailment magnitude and attack speed. Intentional fragility for maximum damage output.
terms.whyItMatters: Defines the build's risk-reward identity. You sacrifice physical defense to become an ailment damage specialist — positioning and ballista distance become your real defense.

dialogue.user: Won't Obsessive Rituals make me too squishy?
dialogue.aiQuestion: It does remove physical defenses, but the ballista summons handle clearing from range. Position carefully and rely on movement skills to survive.

terms.shortDefinition: Barrier mechanic that absorbs damage and recharges over time.
terms.detailedDefinition: A defensive skill unique to the Mercenary that creates a damage-absorbing barrier. The ward recharges gradually over time, providing a reliable layer of damage mitigation without requiring active management.
terms.whyItMatters: Primary defense layer after taking Obsessive Rituals. Compensates for lost Armour/Evasion with a rechargeable damage shield.

dialogue.user: How do I stay alive without Armour?
dialogue.aiThoughts: Player needs defense guidance post-Obsessive Rituals.
dialogue.aiQuestion: Sorcery Ward is your main damage buffer. Keep it topped up during boss fights and use movement to avoid sustained hits.

terms.shortDefinition: Chaos damage over time with base magnitude equal to 20% of Physical + Chaos damage from the hit.
terms.detailedDefinition: An ailment that deals chaos damage over time. The base magnitude captures 20% of the combined Physical and Chaos damage from the triggering hit. Duration scales with attack speed and skill modifiers, allowing multiple overlapping stacks.
terms.whyItMatters: One half of the dual-ailment engine. Poison's chaos damage type bypasses enemy resistance more reliably than elemental ailments at endgame.

dialogue.aiThoughts: Player needs the math explained simply.
dialogue.aiQuestion: Each poison tick equals 20% of your Physical + Chaos hit damage, modified by more/faster poison nodes. Stack multiple hits for overlapping damage.

terms.shortDefinition: Physical damage over time with base magnitude of 15% of Physical damage, doubled while target moves.
terms.detailedDefinition: A physical damage over time ailment. Base magnitude captures 15% of the Physical damage from the triggering hit. Critically, bleeding damage doubles while the affected target is moving, making it exceptionally strong against mobile enemies.
terms.whyItMatters: The other half of the dual-ailment engine. The movement damage multiplier makes bleeding synergize with kiting plays and area denial setups.

dialogue.user: Why does bleeding double when enemies move?
dialogue.aiThoughts: Player curious about the movement multiplier.
dialogue.aiQuestion: It's a built-in design to reward kiting. Circle-strafe bosses and bleed damage spikes — this is your build's core loop.

terms.shortDefinition: The base damage value captured by an ailment before modifiers are applied.
terms.detailedDefinition: The snapshot value that determines how much damage a single ailment instance deals per tick. For poison, magnitude = 20% of (Physical + Chaos) from the hit. For bleeding, magnitude = 15% of Physical from the hit. All % more magnitude modifiers multiply this base value.
terms.whyItMatters: The fundamental stat to optimize. Every damage node in this build funnels into magnitude — higher magnitude means stronger ticks per stack.

dialogue.user: Should I care about magnitude or duration?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Magnitude first, always. Duration only matters to ensure ticks outlast the fight. A high-magnitude short poison outdamages a weak long one.

terms.shortDefinition: Gives more poison magnitude against enemies that are also bleeding.
terms.detailedDefinition: A keystone passive that significantly increases poison magnitude specifically when the target is also affected by bleeding. This creates a conditional damage spike that rewards maintaining both ailments simultaneously.
terms.whyItMatters: Core keystone that justifies the dual-ailment approach. Without it, poison and bleed operate independently. With it, they multiply each other's value.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Poison 3 says 'your poison hits harder when the enemy is also bleeding.' It's the reason this build runs both ailments.

terms.shortDefinition: Gives more bleeding magnitude against enemies that are also poisoned.
terms.detailedDefinition: A keystone passive that significantly increases bleeding magnitude specifically when the target is also affected by poison. Paired with Poison 3, it creates a symmetric dual-ailment amplification loop.
terms.whyItMatters: The mirror keystone to Poison 3. Together they ensure both ailments are always stronger when stacked, making the dual-ailment strategy mandatory rather than optional.

dialogue.user: Do I need both Poison 3 and Bleed 3?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Yes — they feed each other. Poison 3 strengthens poison when bleed is present, and Bleed 3 does the reverse. Dropping one halves the synergy.

terms.shortDefinition: 20% more bleeding magnitude against poisoned enemies and 20% more poison magnitude against bleeding enemies.
terms.detailedDefinition: A support gem that provides bidirectional ailment magnitude bonuses. When linked to a physical attack, it increases bleeding magnitude by 20% on poisoned targets and poison magnitude by 20% on bleeding targets, amplifying the dual-ailment synergy.
terms.whyItMatters: Stacks multiplicatively with Poison 3 and Bleed 3 keystones, creating a compounding damage loop that makes dual ailments dramatically stronger than either alone.

dialogue.aiThoughts: Player evaluating support gem slot usage.
dialogue.aiQuestion: Absolutely — At Mixture stacks with both keystones. It's the cheapest way to spike dual-ailment damage before investing in expensive uniques.

terms.shortDefinition: Fires a bouncing grenade that causes poison gas burst and leaves a growing poison cloud.
terms.detailedDefinition: An attack skill that launches a bouncing grenade, dealing an initial poison gas burst on impact and leaving a poison cloud that grows in radius over time. Excellent for area denial and applying poison to multiple enemies simultaneously.
terms.whyItMatters: Primary clearing and poison-application skill. The growing cloud ensures sustained poison uptime on groups, feeding into the Poison 3 / Bleed 3 synergy.

dialogue.user: Which skill should I use for clearing?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Gas Grenade is your clear skill. Bounce it into dense packs and let the expanding cloud apply poison to everything.

terms.shortDefinition: Fires a rapid volley of projectiles, empowered to repeat multiple times.
terms.detailedDefinition: An attack skill that fires a volley of projectiles in the target direction. When empowered through passive nodes or support gems, Barrage repeats multiple times in a single activation, making it effective for applying bleeding through repeated physical hits.
terms.whyItMatters: Strong single-target and AoE option for applying bleeding. Each projectile attempt is a separate hit chance, maximizing bleed application rate.

dialogue.user: Barrage or Gas Grenade for bosses?
dialogue.aiThoughts: Player choosing between skills for bossing.
dialogue.aiQuestion: Barrage excels at single-target bleed application through repeated hits. Gas Grenade is better for multi-target poison clouds.

terms.shortDefinition: Enemy resource that causes them to flee when depleted; No Mercy scales damage based on missing Concentration.
terms.detailedDefinition: A mechanic present on Expedition and Delve enemies where they possess a Concentration bar. When depleted, the enemy enters a fleeing state, attempting to escape the arena. The No Mercy ascendancy node converts their missing Concentration into More Damage dealt against them.
terms.whyItMatters: The damage-scaling engine for No Mercy. Pushing Concentration to zero maximizes your damage output on bosses that use this mechanic.

dialogue.user: How do I maximize No Mercy damage?
dialogue.aiThoughts: Player wants to optimize the Concentration interaction.
dialogue.aiQuestion: Break the enemy's Concentration bar as fast as possible early in the fight. The lower it is, the higher your No Mercy damage bonus.

terms.shortDefinition: Increases the maximum number of poison stacks maintainable on a single target.
terms.detailedDefinition: A mechanic or node that raises the cap on poison stacks per target. By default, a limited number of poison instances can exist on one enemy. Escalating Poison increases this cap, allowing more simultaneous poison ticks and higher total damage output.
terms.whyItMatters: Directly multiplies poison damage by allowing more stacks. Combined with high magnitude, escalating poison turns single-target encounters into chaos damage fountains.

dialogue.user: How many poison stacks can I have on a boss?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Stack count depends on your Escalating Poison investment. More stacks mean more simultaneous ticks, each dealing magnitude damage.

categories.title: Main Damage Skills
categories.subtitle: Gas Grenade & Barrage
categories.description: Your two primary skills that clear maps through poison DoT stacking and bleed physical damage.
categories.details: Gas Grenade throws a canister that shatters into poison gas clouds, dealing damage over time to enemies caught in the area. Barrage fires a rapid volley of projectiles across the screen, applying bleed through each individual hit. Gas Grenade excels at zone control and sustained DPS, while Barrage provides high attack-speed-driven application rate.
categories.analogy: Gas Grenade is your area-denial toxin, Barrage is your shredding barrage — both stack debuffs relentlessly.
categories.primaryFocus: DoT application rate and cumulative poison/bleed stacking
inScope: Gas Grenade (Lv20) + Elemental Armament, At Mixture, Nova Projectiles, Faster Projectiles, Multifire
Barrage (Lv20) + Bleed 3 supports, At Mixture, Multifire, Faster Attacks, Close Combat
Both benefit from DoT duration, DoT magnitude, and attack speed

categories.title: Support Gems
categories.subtitle: Poison, Bleed, At Mixture & Utility Supports
categories.description: Support gems that amplify your DoT damage, extend duration, and optimize the poison/bleed trade-off.
categories.details: At Mixture is the keystone support — it converts a portion of your poison or bleed damage into the other DoT type, ensuring both debuffs contribute. Elemental Armament converts elemental damage to your chosen element for Gas Grenade. Poison and Bleed supports increase damage per stack independently. Multifire and Faster Projectiles boost application rate across both skills.
categories.analogy: At Mixture is your damage blender — it makes poison and bleed work together instead of competing.
categories.primaryFocus: Maximizing combined DoT output through At Mixture synergy
inScope: At Mixture — converts portion of Poison to Bleed and Bleed to Poison
Elemental Armament (Lightning) for Gas Grenade elemental conversion
Poison 3 supports: Increased Duration, More Damage, Number of Poisons
Bleed 3 supports: Increased Duration, More Physical Damage, Number of Bleeds
Multifire, Faster Projectiles, Faster Attacks for application rate
Culling Strike for boss kill cleanup

categories.title: Defenses
categories.subtitle: Sorcery Ward, Movement Evasion & Flasks
categories.description: Defense layers combining Sorcery Ward barriers, movement-based evasion, and life leech sustainability.
categories.details: Sorcery Ward creates a barrier that absorbs damage and triggers effects when broken, giving you a second layer beyond life. The Witchhunter excels at movement-based evasion through high attack speed and mobility skills. Life flasks with leech recovery form the baseline sustain. Obsessive Rituals trades defense nodes for offense, creating a risk-reward balance you must manage through positioning and Ward uptime.
categories.analogy: Sorcery Ward is your bubble, movement is your insurance, and Obsessive Rituals means you earn your safety through skill.
categories.primaryFocus: Ward barrier management and movement-based survival
inScope: Sorcery Ward barrier (skill + passive investment) for second health pool
Movement speed and evasion rating from Witchhunter passives
Life flasks with quick application and leech recovery
Obsessive Rituals trade-off — defensive passives sacrificed for offensive scaling
Positioning and kiting as primary avoidance

categories.title: Ascendancy
categories.subtitle: Witchhunter — No Mercy, Obsessive Rituals, Sorcery Ward
categories.description: Witchhunter ascendancy nodes that define the build's identity around precision, DoT mastery, and calculated risk.
categories.details: No Mercy is the core node, granting increased damage to affected enemies and scaling with DoT stacks — it rewards sustained engagements and multiple debuffs. Obsessive Rituals removes defensive passive nodes from the tree and converts them to offensive scaling, forcing reliance on Sorcery Ward and movement. Sorcery Ward integration across the ascendancy provides the barrier mechanic that replaces the sacrificed passive defenses.
categories.analogy: You traded safety for lethality — every node you gave up came back as damage, but now you survive through skill and Ward.
categories.primaryFocus: DoT damage scaling through No Mercy with Ward-based survivability
inScope: No Mercy — increased damage to enemies affected by DoTs, scales with stack count
Obsessive Rituals — removes defensive nodes, converts to offensive scaling
Sorcery Ward ascendancy integration for barrier damage absorption
Poison and Bleed-specific ascendancy notables
Attack speed and mobility nodes tied to Witchhunter identity
outOfScope: Ascendancy nodes from other classes (Inquisitor, Ascendant, etc.)

metrics.label: Bleed DPS
metrics.description: Physical damage per second from bleeding. Base magnitude is 15% of physical hit damage, scaled by your bleed magnitude modifiers. Multiplied by 5x for average map damage over duration.
metrics.analogy: Like a deep wound that won't stop flowing—the deeper the cut and the slower the healing, the more blood pours out over time.
inScope: Bleed magnitude scaling
Physical damage conversion to bleed

metrics.label: Poison DPS
metrics.description: Chaos damage per second from poison. Base magnitude is 20% of combined Physical + Chaos hit damage, scaled by poison magnitude modifiers.
metrics.analogy: A spreading toxin that eats away at health—the more potent the venom and the longer it lingers, the greater the toll.
inScope: Poison magnitude scaling
Combined physical and chaos damage

metrics.label: Total DoT DPS
metrics.description: Combined damage per second from both poison and bleed ticking simultaneously on the target.
metrics.analogy: Two wounds working in concert—each independently draining, together overwhelming the target's recovery.
inScope: Simultaneous bleed and poison ticks

metrics.label: Hits to Fill Poison Slots
metrics.description: Number of hits needed to fill all 6 default poison slots on a target. Higher attack speed means faster slot fill.
metrics.analogy: Loading six darts into a spinning wheel—each hit places one dart, and faster spinning means the wheel fills quicker.
inScope: Default 6 poison slot limit
Attack speed to slot fill rate
outOfScope: Increased poison slots from items or skills

scenarios.title: Budget League Starter
scenarios.description: Minimum investment to clear all content with dual DoTs

steps.title: Weapon
steps.description: Bow is the core weapon for Poison + Bleed. Crossbow offers a defensive alternative.

choices.label: Bow
choices.description: Standard bow with Attack Speed and Damage.

pros.title: Better attack speed
pros.description: Faster attacks stack Poison quicker and refresh Bleed more often

pros.title: Wider stat pool
pros.description: More bow uniques and implicit stats support Attack Speed builds

cons.title: No built-in defense
cons.description: Standard bows rarely offer defensive modifiers

choices.whyThisFits: Attack Speed is the priority for Poison stacking. Bow gives the best clear speed foundation.

choices.label: Crossbow

pros.title: Defensive implicit
pros.description: Life on crossbow adds a layer of survivability early

cons.title: Slower attack speed
cons.description: Lower attack speed means slower Poison stacking and Bleed refresh

choices.whenToUse: Viable if struggling with survivability early league, but clear speed will suffer.

steps.title: Body Armour
steps.description: Evasion chest for physical hit mitigation vs Hybrid ES/Evasion for balanced defense.

choices.label: Evasion Chest
choices.description: High Evasion chest piece for maximum physical hit mitigation.

pros.title: Strong physical mitigation
pros.description: Evasion completely negates physical hits when above the threshold

pros.title: Cheaper to find
pros.description: High-evasion bases are common and affordable early league

cons.title: No ES layer
cons.description: Vulnerable to magic hits that bypass Evasion and elemental damage

choices.whyThisFits: Physical hit mitigation is the most important defense layer. Evasion chest maximizes it.

choices.label: Hybrid ES/Evasion Chest
choices.description: Hybrid base with both Energy Shield and Evasion.

pros.title: Dual defense layers
pros.description: Covers both physical hits and elemental/magic damage

cons.title: Lower Evasion value
cons.description: Hybrid bases have less Evasion than pure evasion bases at the same item level

choices.whenToUse: Better mid-to-late league when you can afford well-rolled hybrid bases.

steps.title: Belt
steps.description: RFLAS for Spirit reduction and defense vs Stocking Belt for offense.

choices.label: RFLAS
choices.description: Rare Flat Life And Spirit belt with high Life and Spirit Reservation Reduction.

pros.title: Spirit reservation reduction
pros.description: Frees Spirit budget for more notables and ascendancy nodes

pros.title: Massive Life pool
pros.description: 300+ Life on belt is the best defensive belt option

cons.title: Increases Spirit cost
cons.description: Spirit Reservation Reduction means you spend more Spirit overall

choices.whyThisFits: Spirit budget management is critical. RFLAS enables more defensive nodes while adding Life.

choices.label: Stocking Belt
choices.description: Stocking Belt with Attack Speed and Damage modifiers.

pros.title: Attack speed boost
pros.description: Faster Poison stacking and overall damage output

cons.title: No defensive value
cons.description: Sacrifices a large chunk of Life for offensive stats

choices.whenToUse: When Spirit budget is not a concern and damage is the bottleneck.

steps.title: Flask
steps.description: Life Leech Flask for sustain vs Mana Leech Flask for Spirit efficiency.

choices.label: Life Leech Flask
choices.description: Life Flask with Life Regeneration per second and Life Leech.

pros.title: Active sustain
pros.description: Life Leech provides constant healing during map clears

pros.title: Burst recovery
pros.description: Life Flask charges quickly for emergency survivability

cons.title: No Spirit benefit
cons.description: Does not help with Spirit budget management

choices.whyThisFits: Survivability is the priority for budget builds. Life Leech Flask keeps you alive in tough maps.

choices.label: Mana Leech Flask
choices.description: Mana Flask with Mana Regeneration and Mana Leech.

pros.title: Spirit efficiency
pros.description: Reduces Spirit budget pressure from Spirit-spending nodes

cons.title: No defensive value
cons.description: Loses Life Leech sustain, making maps more dangerous

choices.whenToUse: When Spirit budget is extremely tight and you cannot afford Spirit-reducing gear elsewhere.

scenarios.title: Invested Endgame
scenarios.description: Optimal gear choices for high-tier map clearing and bossing

steps.title: Unique Weapon
steps.description: Serpent's Kiss for Poison damage vs crafted high DPS bow for raw damage.

choices.label: Serpent's Kiss Bow
choices.description: Unique bow with Poison Damage over Time and increased Attack Speed.

pros.title: Massive Poison amplification
pros.description: Increased Poison Damage over Time scales all Poison DoTs significantly

pros.title: Attack Speed synergy
pros.description: Built-in Attack Speed stacks Poison faster and refreshes Bleed more often

cons.title: Higher Spirit cost
cons.description: Spirit Reservation Reduction from unique modifiers increases Spirit spend

steps.title: Unique Chest
steps.description: Body and Soul for Spirit efficiency and survivability vs Abyssus for balanced offense/defense.

choices.label: Body and Soul

pros.title: Spirit budget relief

choices.label: Abyssus
choices.description: Unique chest with Life, Resistance, and Damage over Time multipliers.

pros.title: Balanced offense and defense

steps.title: Rings
steps.description: High-life rings for survivability vs damage-focused rings for raw DPS.

choices.description: Two rings with 90+ Life, Resistances, and Attribute totals.

pros.title: Massive Life pool
pros.description: 180+ Life from two rings is significant survivability

pros.title: Resistance caps
pros.description: Resistances on rings help reach 75% all elements

cons.title: No offensive contribution
cons.description: Purely defensive slots with zero damage modifiers

choices.whyThisFits: Life pool is the most reliable defense layer. Two high-life rings maximize it cheaply.

choices.label: Damage Rings
choices.description: Rings with Damage over Time, Attack Speed, and Critical Strike modifiers.

pros.title: Direct damage boost
pros.description: DoT multipliers and Attack Speed increase overall DPS

cons.title: Reduced survivability
cons.description: Less Life means less room for error in high-tier maps

choices.whenToUse: When survivability is already sufficient and damage is the bottleneck.

steps.title: Helmet
steps.description: Evasion helm for physical mitigation vs Hybrid DoT helm for balanced offense/defense.

choices.label: Evasion Helmet
choices.description: High Evasion helmet with Resistances and Attributes.

pros.title: Physical hit mitigation
pros.description: Evasion on helmet stacks with body armor for near-immunity to physical hits

pros.title: Cheaper to roll
pros.description: Evasion helmets are easier to find with good rolls than hybrid bases

cons.title: No offensive stats
cons.description: Purely defensive item with no damage contribution

choices.whyThisFits: Physical mitigation is the most impactful defense layer. Evasion helm completes the setup.

choices.label: Hybrid DoT Helmet
choices.description: Helmet with DoT multipliers and moderate Evasion.

pros.title: Damage and defense balance
pros.description: DoT multipliers boost Poison and Bleed while maintaining some Evasion

cons.title: Lower Evasion value

choices.whenToUse: When you need a damage boost and can afford reduced physical mitigation.

props.title: Your Witchhunter Journey
props.intro: You've chosen the Poison + Bleed Witchhunter build for this league. Your decisions will shape your success.

start.prompt: League day 1. You've created your Witchhunter. What's your first priority?

choices.text: Find a Bow with Attack Speed and Physical Damage
Rush to the passive tree for Poison and Bleed clusters

bow-found.prompt: You have a decent bow. What support gems are you linking?

choices.text: Poison 3 + Bleed 3 + At Mixture for dual DoT synergy
Raw damage supports like Elemental Damage

tree-first-bad.prompt: You skipped gearing and went straight to the tree. Your attacks tickle without proper damage.

choices.text: Go back and get proper weapon and DoT supports

dot-ready.prompt: Dual DoTs are ticking beautifully. What's your endgame defense strategy?

choices.text: Sorcery Ward + constant movement for evasion
Ignore Obsessive Rituals and stack Armour/Evasion

raw-damage-path.prompt: Your hits hard but you're missing the dual DoT synergy multiplier.

choices.text: Reroll gems to include At Mixture and dual ailment supports

stage.prompt: What stage of the league are you at?

choices.rationale: Early league priorities differ from endgame.

choices.text: A Bow with Physical Damage and Attack Speed

leaf.recommendation: Link Poison 3, Bleed 3, and At Mixture into your bow immediately.
leaf.explanation: With a physical bow, you can apply both Bleed and Poison. At Mixture creates the dual-DoT synergy where each ailment boosts the other's magnitude by 20%. Focus on reaching the Poison and Bleed clusters in the passive tree.
tradeoffs: Early game, prioritize ailment chance over magnitude — consistent application matters more
Take No Mercy ascendancy node first for Concentration-based damage bonus
Budget flasks: Life Leech flask is your best early survival tool

leaf.recommendation: Find any Bow with Physical Damage. Attack Speed is the priority stat.
leaf.explanation: You need a bow for this build. Any physical bow works league start. Avoid bows with only elemental damage — you need Physical for Bleed. Attack Speed > Raw Damage early game because more hits = more DoT applications.
tradeoffs: A cheap 1-socket bow with At Mixture is better than a 6L without it
Gradually upgrade: more sockets → more supports → exponential DoT growth

leaf.recommendation: Rush Poison and Bleed magnitude clusters in the passive tree.
leaf.explanation: Without tree allocation, your DoTs underperform. Allocate to the nearest Poison and Bleed notables first, then extend toward magnitude and duration clusters. The dual-DoT synergy from At Mixture scales with tree investment.
tradeoffs: Short allocation to key nodes > long allocation to mediocre nodes
Consider using a Vaal orb to relocate your start if stuck

choices.text: Fast map clearing and efficient farming

leaf.recommendation: Maximize clear speed with Gas Grenade cloud coverage and high Attack Speed.
leaf.explanation: For mapping, you want screen-filling poison clouds from Gas Grenade while Barrage applies Bleed. Stack Attack Speed, Area of Effect, and DoT duration. RFLAS belt + Body and Soul + two life rings for safe mapping.
tradeoffs: Clear speed > single-target in mapping builds — more maps cleared = more profit
Gas Grenade clouds persist and overlap, creating AoE poison zones
Movement speed is implicit DPS — faster mapping = more clears per hour

leaf.recommendation: Shift to maximum single-target DoT magnitude with crafted modifiers.
leaf.explanation: Uber bosses require sustained single-target DoT. Craft 'More Magnitude of Poison' and 'More Magnitude of Bleeding' on your gear. Stack Duration over Clear Speed. No Mercy becomes critical as boss Concentration drains. Sorcery Ward is mandatory for survival.
tradeoffs: Single-target focus means terrible clear — use a separate clearing skill or accept slow mapping
Crafted 'More%' modifiers are worth the investment for Uber attempts
Practice boss mechanics — Obsessive Rituals leaves you fragile
